Fact.Name: Social Security (OASDI) wage base TY2026
Fact.Description: TY2026 OASDI contribution and benefit base = $184,500. #166: SSA, "Cost-of-Living Increase and Other Determinations for 2026", 90 FR 49047 (Nov. 3, 2025), https://www.federalregister.gov/d/2025-19763 (PDF https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/FR-2025-11-03/pdf/2025-19763.pdf), p. 49050: "The OASDI contribution and benefit base is $184,500 for remuneration paid in 2026 and self-employment income earned in tax years beginning in 2026."

Fact.Name: SE tax filing threshold
Fact.Description: Net earnings from self-employment of $400 or more generally require Schedule SE / SE tax. Cite: 26 U.S.C. § 1402; Schedule SE instructions.

Fact.Name: Net profit subject to SE tax before 92.35%
Fact.Description: Positive Schedule C net profit subject to SE tax (MVP: no farm/optional methods). Cite: 26 U.S.C. § 1402(a); Schedule SE.

Fact.Name: Net earnings from self-employment
Fact.Description: Schedule SE: net profit × 92.35% (0.9235). Cite: Schedule SE instructions (multiply by 92.35%); reflects employer-equivalent portion already excluded via the 7.65% reduction embedded in 92.35% (= 100% − 7.65%). Authority: 26 U.S.C. § 1402(a)(12): deduction "equal to the product of (A) the taxpayer's net earnings from self-employment ... and (B) one-half of the sum of the rates imposed by subsections (a) and (b) of section 1401" = 1 - (12.4% + 2.9%) / 2 = 0.9235. Rational 9235/10000 = 0.9235.

Fact.Name: SE tax applies
Fact.Description: True when net earnings from SE ≥ $400. Cite: Schedule SE; 26 U.S.C. § 1402.

Fact.Name: Primary filer total OASDI wages (W-2 Box 3)
Fact.Description: Sum of primary filer W-2 social security wages for Schedule SE wage-base coordination. Cite: Schedule SE — Social Security wages reduce remaining wage base for the 12.4% portion.

Fact.Name: Primary filer total Social Security tips (W-2 Box 7)
Fact.Description: Sum of primary filer W-2 box 7 social security tips. Schedule SE line 8a is "Total social security wages and tips (total of boxes 3 and 7 on Form(s) W-2)". Cite: 26 U.S.C. § 1402(b)(1); 2025/2026 Instructions for Schedule SE, line 8.

Fact.Name: Remaining Social Security wage base for SE
Fact.Description: max(0, TY2026 wage base $184,500 − (W-2 box 3 OASDI wages + W-2 box 7 OASDI tips)). Schedule SE line 8 (8a W-2 boxes 3 + 7; 8b Form 4137 and 8c Form 8919 are out of scope: Form 8919 wages are hard-coded $0 in income.xml and 4137-type tips are not collected). Cite: 26 U.S.C. § 1402(b)(1); Instructions for Schedule SE, line 8; TY2026 wage base: see /socialSecurityWageBaseTy2026 (90 FR 49047, p. 49050).

Fact.Name: Schedule SE line 8a: Total social security wages and tips
Fact.Description: #89. 2026 draft Schedule SE (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-dft/f1040sse--dft.pdf, created 4/27/26), form page 1, line 8a: "Total social security wages and tips (total of boxes 3 and 7 on Form(s) W-2) and railroad retirement (tier 1) compensation." W-2 box 3 (/primaryFilerOasdiWagesTotal) plus box 7 (/primaryFilerOasdiTipsTotal) for the person with self-employment income; railroad retirement compensation is not collected. Wage-base coordination under 26 U.S.C. 1402(b)(1). Printed only; the tax itself uses /seRemainingSocialSecurityWageBase.

Fact.Name: Schedule SE line 8d
Fact.Description: #89. 2026 draft Schedule SE (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-dft/f1040sse--dft.pdf), form page 1, line 8d: "Add lines 8a, 8b, and 8c." Line 8b (Form 4137 unreported tips) stops the return (unreportedTips /flowKnockoutUnreportedTips) and line 8c (Form 8919 wages) has no input (income /wagesFrom8919 is $0), so line 8d = line 8a. Line 8a says "If $184,500 or more, skip lines 8b through 10, and go to line 11", so line 8d is $0 (printed blank) when line 8a is at least the TY2026 wage base (/socialSecurityWageBaseTy2026, $184,500; 90 FR 49047, p. 49050; 26 U.S.C. 1402(b)(1)).

Fact.Name: SE earnings subject to 12.4% Social Security tax
Fact.Description: Lesser of net earnings from SE and remaining Social Security wage base. Rate authority: 26 U.S.C. § 1401(a) — 12.4% on self-employment income. Quote (§ 1401(a)): "a tax equal to 12.4 percent of the amount of the self-employment income…" https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/1401

Fact.Name: Social Security portion of SE tax
Fact.Description: 12.4% × SE Social Security taxable earnings. Cite: 26 U.S.C. § 1401(a). Rational 124/1000 = 0.124.

Fact.Name: SE earnings subject to 2.9% Medicare tax
Medicare (HI) portion of SE tax
Fact.Description: 2.9% × SE Medicare taxable earnings. Cite: 26 U.S.C. § 1401(b). Rational 29/1000 = 0.029. Note: Additional 0.9% Medicare tax above threshold is OUT OF SCOPE in this slice (explicit).

Fact.Name: Self-employment tax
Fact.Description: Total SE tax = Social Security portion + Medicare portion. Schedule SE → Schedule 2 (other taxes) → Form 1040. Cite: 26 U.S.C. § 1401; Schedule SE instructions.

Fact.Name: Deductible part of self-employment tax
Fact.Description: Employer-equivalent portion = one-half of SE tax. Schedule 1 adjustment. Cite: 26 U.S.C. § 164(f) — https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/164#f Quote (§ 164(f)(1)): "there shall be allowed as a deduction for the taxable year an amount equal to one-half of the taxes imposed by section 1401 (other than the taxes imposed by section 1401(b)(2))". Flows to Schedule 1 line 15 → /adjustmentsToIncome (taxCalculations.xml).

Fact.Name: Schedule C section complete
Fact.Description: Interview complete for Schedule C MVP (or filer had no SE income).
